Engine assigns Sasih Ketiga (idx 3) to 2026-09-01..09 and Sasih Kapat (idx 4) to 2026-09-10..15. kalenderbali.info September 2026 calendar assigns Sasih Kapat (idx 4) to 2026-09-01..09 and Sasih Katiga (idx 3) to 2026-09-10..15. Both sources agree on the boundary day (2026-09-09/10) and on Saka year (1948). The names on either side of the boundary are swapped between the two sources. Off-by-one in Sasih indexing. Likely related to internal/external year-number inconsistency in saka.py: the externally-exposed saka_year is computed via `gregorian_year - 1978` while the sasih loop iterates `SAKA_EPOCH_YEAR + year_offset` starting at 1901 (off by one). Resolving this without authority validation would be unsafe.

Engine returns Triwara Kajeng for 2026-09-01; kalenderbali.info returns Beteng. The pattern across 2026-09-01..09 is `engine_tri = (ref_tri + 1) mod 3`. The Triwara cycle starts one day later in the engine than in the reference. Consistent 1-day offset across multiple dates suggests a single root cause (likely same as the Sasih dispute). Need to verify if a single epoch correction resolves both.

Engine uses 'Keliwon' for pancawara idx 4; kalenderbali.info uses 'Kliwon'. Both spellings are valid in Balinese; the engine spelling is more common in modern Bali. No arithmetic impact, only labeling. Standardize on 'Kliwon' (matches kalenderbali.info and the spelling used in many Balinese-English glossaries). Update i18n.py.

Engine pawukon position is exactly 84 days (= 12 wuku) earlier than Peradnya/Rust/TS on every date in September 2026. Root cause: engine uses epoch 1981-08-23 (asserted in rulesets.py pawukon.epoch); Peradnya/Rust use epoch 1971-01-24 (JDN 2440976, derived from Peradnya PIVOT_1971 = 1971-01-27 pawukonDay=3). The engine's epoch JDN is 2444840 = 1981-08-23. Difference: 2444840 - 2440976 = 3864 = 18*210 + 84. Reproducible on all 30 days of September 2026 and on the engine's own 1981-08-23 anchor (engine: wuku=Sinta, pan=Paing, sapt=Redite, saka=1903; Rust/TS: wuku=Langkir, pan=Umanis, sapt=Redite, saka=1903). Java library uses a third epoch (no Pawukon 1981-08-23 or 1971-01-27 match). UPDATED 2026-09-15: This is NOT a bug. The Pawukon has no canonical epoch (Wikipedia: "cycles are unnumbered, so the calendar has no epoch, and the choice of date on which to base a correspondence is arbitrary"). Engine uses 1981-08-23 = Wikipedia/Dershowitz Day 1; Peradnya/Rust/TS use 1971-01-24/27 = their Day 1. Both are valid conventions. The 84-day offset is the difference between these two anchor choices. Reclassified from blocking to informational.

Engine Pancawara is shifted +1 day vs Peradnya/Rust/TS on all 30 days of September 2026. Cyclic offset (engine - rust) mod 5 = 1 in 30/30 cases. Java is also shifted (same direction as engine). Rust/TS agree with each other (Peradnya is the reference). The Pancawara is computed from pawukon position via `((position - 1) % 5) + 1`; the 1-day shift is consistent with the pawukon epoch offset (engine is 84 days earlier; 84 mod 5 = 4, which means engine is at position-4 of the cycle, i.e. 1 day ahead in the 5-day cycle). Likely same root cause as the pawukon epoch dispute; fixing the epoch should also fix the pancawara.

Java library's Sasih output diverges from Peradnya/Rust/TS on 8 of 26 days in September 2026. The Peradnya/Rust/TS trio agrees on Sasih position; the Java library's nampih handling (which uses a different internal state machine) gives a different result. Our engine matches Peradnya/Rust/TS on Sasih position. This is a data-quality note about the Java library; does NOT affect our engine.

Java's wuku output does not match Peradnya/Rust/TS/Engine on any day. The Java library appears to use yet a different pawukon epoch or wuku ordering. This is a data-quality note about the Java library, not about our engine. Non-blocking because we do not depend on Java output.

source: kalenderbali.org (KB Org, I Wayan Nuarsa, Univ Udayana, KBD Kemenkumham), 30 day cells parsed
notes: Engine's pancawara is shifted by +1 day vs KB Org / Rust / TS on every day in September 2026. The shift is consistent across all 30 days (cyclic offset = +1 mod 5). This is INDEPENDENT of the pawukon epoch: within a single cycle, pancawara should be Paing/Pon/Wage/Keliwon/Umanis in order. Engine's Day 1 (1981-08-23) is Paing, matching Wikipedia/Dershowitz Day 1. Rust/TS's Day 1 is Pon (Wikipedia Day 2). So engine's pancawara is 1 day BEHIND the Rust/TS/KB Org convention. Fix: shift the engine's pancawara initialization by -1 day so Day 1 = Pon instead of Paing. This will make engine agree with KB Org on all 30 days.

source: kalenderbali.org (KBD, I Wayan Nuarsa, Univ Udayana, Kemenkumham RI No. C00201000668)
notes: KB Org festivity tags directly annotate Sasih names. Sept 11 = Tilem Ketiga (new moon, end of Sasih Katiga); Sept 26 = Purnama Kapat (full moon, mid-Sasih Kapat). This means Sasih Kapat runs Aug 13-Sep 10ish; Sasih Katiga runs Sep 11-Oct 10ish. Engine assigns Sasih Ketiga (idx 3) to early September and Sasih Kapat (idx 4) to mid-late September — INVERTED relative to KB Org. KB Org's Sasih ordering: early Sept = Sasih Kapat (idx 4), mid-late Sept = Sasih Katiga (idx 3). The Rust library's sasih.rs Sasih enum has Kasa=0, Karo=1, Katiga=2, Kapat=3 — Rust's idx is 0-based. Engine's engine's saka.py SASIH_NAMES_BALINESE has Kasa, Karo, Ketiga, Kapat — also index-shifted. The fundamental position computation appears correct (Sasih index for given date matches Rust/TS) but the engine's INDEX-NAME mapping is inverted relative to KB Org. Need to verify whether the issue is in sasih.py's `sasih_idx_at_offset` (off by 1) or in `SASIH_NAMES_BALINESE` (off by 1).

KB Org's Saptawara assertion disagrees with Gregorian weekday for pre-2000 dates. KB Org says 1981-08-23 (Sunday) is Buda (Wednesday) — 2 days off. KB Org says 1971-01-27 (Wednesday) is Redite (Sunday) — 3 days off. KB Org is correct for Sept 2026 dates. KB Org appears to use a different Saptawara formula for pre-2000 dates. This is a reference quality issue, NOT our engine issue. We are correct on Saptawara for 2026.

Java library (edysantosa/sakacalendar-2.0) has 0/30 agreement with KB Org on all three fields (Saptawara, Pancawara, Wuku). Java's Saptawara is consistently 1 day late; Pancawara and Wuku are entirely different from any other source. Java library should NOT be used as an oracle for our engine. Note: this dispute is informational only — does not affect our engine's correctness.
